title: Bearing Wrongs
note: He defines this as bearing it, and not doing the same back, when someone wrongs you for some cause or out of ignorance. It follows the chapter on another’s wife, to say you must bear even with those who leave the path.

couplets.plain: As the earth holds up those who dig into it, the highest thing is to bear with those who scorn you.
couplets.pm: As the earth holds up those who dig it and doesn’t let them fall, bearing with those who scorn you is the foremost righteousness. Scorn covers both what is done and what is said beyond measure.

links.quote: bear with those who scorn you
the earth holds up those who dig into it
links.reason: The earth holding up the very people who dig into it is the whole model of patience.

couplets.plain: Always bear a wrong done to you. Forgetting it is better still.
couplets.pm: Since patience is good, bear what others do beyond measure even when you have the power to punish. Better than that is to forget it at once and not take it in. While you bear a wrong you still hold it in mind, which is why forgetting is better.
couplets.sensitive: urges always forgiving and forgetting harm

links.reason: Sets a higher step above bearing a wrong: not remembering it at all.

couplets.plain: The deepest poverty is to turn a guest away. The greatest strength is to bear with fools.
couplets.pm: The poverty of all poverty is refusing to receive guests. In the same way, the strength of all strength is bearing with those who wrong you out of ignorance. Turning guests away is unrighteous and never counts as wealth, and bearing with fools is never weakness but strength.
couplets.sensitive: Counsel to bear with others, as in the rest of the chapter.

links.quote: The greatest strength is to bear with fools
links.reason: Puts bearing with fools at the very top of all strength.

links.quote: The deepest poverty is to turn a guest away
links.reason: Turning a guest away is named the deepest form of being poor.

couplets.plain: If you want your integrity never to leave you, guard your patience and live by it.
couplets.pm: Someone who wants their integrity never to leave them must guard their patience so that it doesn’t perish. There is no nobility except through patience.

links.quote: guard your patience and live by it
links.reason: Keeping your integrity is made to depend on guarding your patience.

couplets.plain: Those who punish a wrong are counted as nothing. Those who bear it are wrapped up and kept like gold.
couplets.pm: The wise give no place in their minds to those who can’t bear an injury and punish the one who did it, since they have become no better than that person. Those who bear it they keep like wrapped gold, thinking of them without pause for their nobility.
couplets.sensitive: praises forgiving those who do you harm

links.quote: Those who punish a wrong are counted as nothing
links.reason: People who pay back a wrong are counted as nothing at all.

links.quote: Those who bear it are wrapped up and kept like gold
links.reason: Whoever bears a wrong is treasured the way gold is kept.

couplets.plain: Those who punish have one day’s pleasure. Those who bear it have renown until the end.
couplets.pm: Those who punish the one who harmed them get only that one day’s pleasure, a false pleasure, gloating that they did what they set out to do. Those who bear it have renown until the world perishes, since renown can end only when the world that holds it ends.
couplets.note: பொன்றும் துணையும் says only “until it perishes”. He supplies the world. It could as well be the person’s own death.
couplets.sensitive: urges forgiving rather than answering an injury

links.quote: Those who punish have one day’s pleasure
Those who bear it have renown until the end
links.reason: Against that single day, the one who bears a wrong has renown to the end.

couplets.plain: Even if others do you wrongs that should never be done, it is good to suffer the pain and do nothing unrighteous.
couplets.pm: Even if others do you cruel things that should never be done, it is good to grieve for the suffering this will bring them and to do nothing unrighteous yourself. That grief is pity, that they may fall into the fires of hell.
couplets.note: நோ நொந்து can be your own pain, as the plain reading takes it. He makes it grief for the wrongdoers, for what they will suffer.

links.quote: suffer the pain and do nothing unrighteous
links.reason: Asks you to take the pain of even the worst wrong and still do no wrong back.

couplets.plain: Defeat by your own worth those who wrong you in their arrogance.
couplets.pm: Those who do you harm out of pride, defeat by your patience. Don’t lose by doing harm to them in turn. Rise above them through patience and win.

links.reason: Turns an injury into a contest won by your own worth, not by paying it back.

couplets.plain: Those who can bear cruel words from the mouths of people who overstep are as pure as those who renounce the world.
couplets.pm: Even while living the household life, those who bear the cruel words of people who have left the path are as pure as renouncers. Purity means a mind without stain. He says “mouths” to show how low a person is whose mouth is used to such words.
couplets.note: துறந்தாரின் can mean “like those who renounce” or “more than those who renounce”. He takes the first, and the plain reading follows him.

links.quote: bear cruel words from the mouths of people who overstep
links.reason: Those who bear cruel words are set beside the renouncers for purity.

couplets.plain: Those who fast and endure it are great, but they come after those who endure the cruel words of others.
couplets.pm: Those who give up food under vows and bear the pain are greater than all others. But their greatness comes after those who bear the cruel words of the ignorant, because these people endure while still held by the two attachments that work against enduring.

links.quote: they come after those who endure the cruel words of others
links.reason: Even the hard discipline of fasting ranks behind bearing cruel words.

ideaLinks.quote: Those who punish have one day’s pleasure. Those who bear it have renown until the end
ideaLinks.reason: Sets the one day’s pleasure of punishing against the lasting renown of bearing a wrong.

ideaLinks.quote: Those who bear it have renown until the end
ideaLinks.reason: The one who bears a wrong is promised renown that lasts.
